feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
entry.summary:
Trajectory2Gym synthesizes tool-use agent supervision by constructing executable interactions around under-supported compositional structures and filtering for actions grounded in the agent's visible interaction history.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that scaling tool-use agents requires constructing learnable, decision-grounded interaction environments rather than merely collecting successful raw trajectories.

entry.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
entry.summary:
StreamVibe introduces a benchmark, streaming vision-language model, and hierarchical memory harness designed to infer implicit, dynamic user intents and improve proactive video interactions.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language models to proactively assist users during real-time tasks without requiring continuous explicit prompts or losing track of changing context.

entry.title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
entry.summary:
DynaFlow introduces free-form executable workflow synthesis into a main agent's action space, enabling dynamically generated, code-based multi-agent orchestration without fine-tuning sub-agents.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that training a single agent to dynamically write program-based orchestration flows significantly outperforms static multi-agent architectures without needing to retrain underlying sub-agent executors.

entry.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
entry.summary:
InteractiveWorld is the first verifiable environment for closed-loop human-AI interaction, featuring InteractiveBench to evaluate MLLM assistants across 120 multi-turn tasks using state-based rewards.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized, reproducible platform to test and advance egocentric MLLMs for real-world physical assistance without relying on costly human trials.

entry.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
entry.summary:
This paper presents a system-level framework for work agents, defining execution across stateful workspaces, task classifications, core capability families, and optimization strategies for models and runtime harnesses.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified framework for designing, optimizing, and evaluating AI agents to reliably execute complex, verifiable work in real-world digital environments.

entry.title: Spatial Audio Generation and Editing with Executable Plans and Self-Distilling Transfusion
entry.summary:
AMBIT is a unified framework for First-Order Ambisonics generation and editing using a shared Transfusion backbone, an FOA-aware continuous VAE, and joint on-policy self-distillation.

Why it matters: It improves source preservation and spatial quality in native FOA audio editing and generation, allowing precise instruction-guided manipulation of 3D soundscapes.

entry.title: Principia: Test-Time Hypotheses to Principle Construction for Scientific Discovery
entry.summary:
Principia is an LLM-based framework that constructs, applies, and continually refines task-specific comparative causal hypotheses and inductive scientific principles directly at test time using ongoing observations.

Why it matters: It automates the labor-intensive hypotheses-to-principle translation stage, allowing language models to continuously evolve scientific domain knowledge directly during inference across complex discovery benchmarks.

entry.title: Δτ-Bench: Pushing Agents Toward a Moving Capability
entry.summary:
Δτ-Bench is an executable agent benchmark containing 1,588 multi-turn tasks across 42 domains designed to evaluate LLM agent adaptation to evolving tool ecosystems.

Why it matters: It exposes the fragility of current LLM agents and skill-learning techniques when operating in real-world software environments with constantly changing API tools.

entry.title: Qwen-Image-PE: Learning Visual Design for Text-to-Image Prompt Enhancement
entry.summary:
Qwen-Image-PE enhances text-to-image prompts using a two-stage training strategy with Caption-Based Reverse Distillation and Groupwise Design Reward to improve fine-grained visual design.

Why it matters: It establishes an open-weights method for prompt expansion that systematically optimizes specific design dimensions and generalizes across diverse downstream text-to-image models.

entry.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement in the Era of Large Models: Foundation, Risks, Evaluation and Open Challenges
entry.summary:
This survey provides an operational definition and process framework for trustworthy recursive self-improvement (RSI) in large models, categorizing requirements across four interconnected themes and three evaluative perspectives.

Why it matters: As large models autonomously modify their own prompts, tools, and update mechanisms, structured frameworks for trustworthy RSI are necessary to prevent catastrophic alignment failure, capability degradation, and lost human oversight.

entry.title: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
entry.summary:
AV-FABLE is a new dual-timeline benchmark containing 998 hours of long-form audio-visual videos designed to evaluate localized, sparse AI manipulations across independent audio and visual timelines.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard language outputs from AV-LLMs fail to report deepfakes despite encoding the necessary forensic features, providing a framework to extract accurate multimodal temporal localization.

entry.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
entry.summary:
HiP3R introduces a training-free hierarchical pose graph that resolves camera drift and coordinate inconsistency in long-horizon 3D reconstruction from feed-forward models.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, globally consistent 3D reconstruction and accurate camera trajectory estimation for long video sequences containing thousands of frames without retraining existing models.

entry.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
S3AC introduces a critic-training recipe and Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling for LLM reasoning, outperforming critic-free methods across models up to 397B parameters.

Why it matters: It enables stable actor-critic reinforcement learning for long chain-of-thought reasoning, avoiding the rollout waste and performance degradation of critic-free baseline approaches.

entry.title: EmbodiedLab: Benchmarking Embodied Agents That Act to Know
entry.summary:
EmbodiedLab is a benchmark containing 30 physics-simulated science experiments designed to evaluate embodied agents on tasks where physical manipulation is required to acquire unknown scientific knowledge.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between traditional manipulation benchmarks and scientific discovery benchmarks by requiring agents to execute physical experimentation to discover dynamic parameters.

entry.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
entry.summary:
RynnVLA-Latent enables cross-embodiment robot pretraining by extracting 3D-grounded continuous latent actions from unlabeled videos, bypassing the need for native action labels.

Why it matters: It removes the bottleneck of scarce action-labeled robot datasets by allowing policies to pretrain on abundant, heterogeneous human and simulation videos.

entry.title: CANS: Capability-Preserving Neuron Steering for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Capability-Preserving Neuron Steering (CANS) is a training-free framework that uses closed-form neuron-wise scaling coefficients to dynamically control LLM behavior while preserving general model capabilities.

Why it matters: CANS provides an efficient, training-free method to safely steer model behaviors without incurring inference-time latency or significantly degrading general capabilities.

entry.title: Test-Time Confidence Adaptation under RL-Induced Trajectory Shift
entry.summary:
StaR-TTA enables test-time confidence adaptation for post-reinforcement-learning LLMs by exploiting a preserved relationship where stable reasoning trajectories remain more likely to yield correct answers without target labels.

Why it matters: It provides a label-free method to maintain reliable confidence estimates for LLM reasoning outputs after the models undergo trajectory-shifting reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Skill$^{\infty}$: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Skill Optimization
entry.summary:
Skill$^{\infty}$ introduces a recursive self-improvement framework where a meta-agent uses a task-decoupled meta-skill to optimize task skills, while recursively optimizing the meta-skill using the exact same procedure.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a practical mechanism for recursive self-improvement by enabling language agents to autonomously optimize both task-level procedural knowledge and the meta-level procedures used to refine that knowledge.

entry.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
entry.summary:
FOCUS is an agentic reinforcement learning method that uses selective branching and active critic learning to improve value estimation and credit assignment in long-horizon language model tasks.

Why it matters: FOCUS solves the credit assignment problem in long-horizon LLM tasks by efficiently targeting compute toward uncertain state value estimates rather than using uniform, high-cost continuation sampling.

entry.title: Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Selective Tie Learning, a method using implicit reward margins and curvature approximations to select optimal tie data for reducing spurious correlations in preference optimization.

Why it matters: It enables more data-efficient preference tuning of language models by strategically selecting tie samples to eliminate shortcut learning without uniform dataset expansion.

entry.title: S3AC: Stabilized, Selective, and Scalable Actor-Critic for LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
S3AC introduces a practical critic-training recipe alongside Difficulty-Aware Prompt Sampling to enable stable token-level credit assignment and prompt selection for LLM chain-of-thought reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that stabilized critic-based actor-critic methods can outperform critic-free baseline approaches like GRPO in large-scale LLM reasoning tasks while maintaining single-rollout efficiency.

entry.title: GPDPO: Learning from Reward Conflicts via Group Pareto-Dominance Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Group Pareto-Dominance Policy Optimization (GPDPO) resolves multi-reward conflicts in LLM alignment by extracting auxiliary pairwise preference signals from Pareto-dominance relations in conflict-filtered rollouts.

Why it matters: GPDPO maximizes sample efficiency in multi-reward LLM alignment by converting otherwise discarded conflicting rollouts into useful preference supervision.

entry.title: Amplify, Locate, Estimate (ALE) on Rare-Failure Rates of Fine-Tuned LLMs
entry.summary:
Amplify, Locate, Estimate (ALE) is a method that efficiently estimates rare safety-fine-tuning failure probabilities by amplifying failure rates via token log-probability changes and extrapolating back using a score-function estimator.

Why it matters: ALE enables accurate measurement of extremely rare LLM safety failures without incurring the prohibitive computational cost of direct sampling.

entry.title: LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
LoopFold accelerates looped Transformers by using a lightweight predictor and corrector to compute multiple recurrent depths in parallel for the same token prefix, reducing decoding latency.

Why it matters: It enables deeper, more accurate looped Transformer architectures to overcome sequential recurrent depth bottlenecks and achieve lower inference latency.

entry.title: StateLoop: Persistent State for Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
StateLoop introduces a persistent, token-wise state with learned gating to improve parameter-efficient looped Transformers by carrying information across deep iterations.

Why it matters: StateLoop enhances the performance and capability of parameter-efficient looped Transformers without requiring deeper parameter footprints as recurrent depth grows.

entry.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
entry.summary:
A new survey proposes world modeling as a unifying framework to categorize video foundation model literature across four core operations: reading, writing, sharing, and interacting.

Why it matters: Structuring video models around latent world states rather than surface pixel dynamics guides the development of models capable of robust physical reasoning and interactive downstream decision-making.

entry.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
entry.summary:
UserArena introduces a real-world e-commerce interactive benchmark for long-horizon recommendation agents alongside On-Policy Trajectory Distillation (OPTD) to align user simulators with production A/B test outcomes.

Why it matters: It enables reliable, offline trajectory-level evaluation of interactive agentic recommendation systems by bridging the gap between simulation fidelity and real-world production A/B test results.

entry.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
entry.summary:
HiSTEVE 1.0 is a hierarchical vision-language-action (VLA) agent for Minecraft that pairs native keyboard-and-mouse control with a VLM planner and capability-aware agent harness for long-horizon task execution.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between high-level autonomous planning and low-level native GUI/non-GUI controls in open-world games without relying on environment APIs or predefined hardcoded skills.

entry.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
entry.summary:
RynnUnify is a 16B unified embodied model that integrates spatial reasoning, long-horizon visual planning via interleaved video-language generation, and robot action execution within a single framework.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a single foundation model can bridge high-level multimodal understanding, visual predictive world-modeling, and low-level physical robot control.

entry.title: RSIHub: A Composable Framework for Agent-Evolution Methods
entry.summary:
RSIHub is an open-source, composable framework that standardizes agent-evolution methods by separating evolution policies into reusable recipes and operators while managing execution, recovery, evaluation, and lineage.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized infrastructure for researchers to reliably compare, track lineage for, and develop agent-evolution algorithms without reinventing underlying execution and evaluation pipelines.

entry.title: Every Weight Is a Path of Shared Discrete Decisions
entry.summary:
TWIG is a neural network weight representation where every weight is a path of inherited discrete decisions, reducing circuit addition costs and unifying compression techniques into a single optimization problem.

Why it matters: TWIG simplifies hardware deployment on chips with fixed weights by eliminating dedicated multipliers and provides a unified framework for model compression.

entry.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
entry.summary:
Dual Exam evaluates Multimodal Agents and World Models independently using fixed environment responses and action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains.

Why it matters: Component-level diagnostic evaluations are necessary because current state-of-the-art agents and world models fail to achieve task success when directly coupled.

entry.title: DirCast: Live Esports Directing and Commentary with a Single Streaming Video-Language Model
entry.summary:
DirCast is a single streaming video-language model that performs real-time live esports camera directing and commentary simultaneously using only raw player camera feeds and past context.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a single streaming model can autonomously produce and commentate on complex live multi-camera broadcasts using only unedited raw video streams and bounded historical context.

entry.title: TenetBench: A Clause-Anchored Russian Corpus for Evaluating Language Models against Professional Codes of Ethics
entry.summary:
TenetBench is a clause-anchored Russian corpus and automated pipeline containing 3,433 ethical rule-conflicting requests paired with benign twins to evaluate how large language models adhere to professional codes of ethics.

Why it matters: It enables targeted evaluation of LLM compliance with specific professional ethics codes and provides an automated framework to generate custom diagnostic datasets for specialized domains.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A new framework reformulates on-policy self-distillation as self-training using fully synthetic queries and privileged reasoning traces generated from high-level topic descriptions without human supervision.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that foundation models can continuously self-improve across multimodal domains without requiring curated datasets or stronger external supervision.

entry.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation
entry.summary:
DraMaze is a multi-agent pipeline using trope memory-guided tree search and narrative backward-dependency memory to generate diverse, coherent microdrama scripts up to 60,000 words.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to generate ultra-long, 60k-word creative scripts without succumbing to narrative repetition or losing long-range plot coherence.

entry.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
MultiAgent-OPD presents an end-to-end framework using on-policy distillation from a frozen teacher model alongside reinforcement learning to jointly train hierarchical Leader-Searcher-Answerer multi-agent systems.

Why it matters: It solves credit assignment challenges in multi-agent reinforcement learning by substituting subjective LLM judges with objective process supervision derived from a trained teacher.

entry.title: MMVistaReason: Toward Open-Data and Post-Training Recipes for Multimodal Reasoning
entry.summary:
MMVistaReason is an open-data post-training recipe combining structured dataset filtering, specialize-then-integrate RL experts, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) to achieve state-of-the-art multimodal reasoning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that systematic open-data processing and capacity-aware post-training allow smaller multimodal models to outperform significantly larger instruction-tuned baselines.

entry.title: Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders
entry.summary:
A new pipeline converts fine-tuned neural AI-text detectors into auditable classifiers by training sparse autoencoders on the residual stream, filtering for high-fidelity interpretable features, and training a lightweight model on those features.

Why it matters: This method enables transparent, highly accurate AI text detection suitable for high-stakes deployment in areas like peer review, education, and content moderation without sacrificing performance.

entry.title: LoCA: Enabling Multi-Modality in Geospatial Location Encoders
entry.summary:
LoCA introduces a two-stage multi-view contrastive framework that overcomes structural low-rank theoretical limits in Lipschitz geospatial location encoders by using co-aligned, high-rank multimodal image targets.

Why it matters: LoCA provides a theoretically grounded method to map single geospatial coordinates to diverse multimodal targets, significantly improving downstream performance across broad earth observation and climate tasks.

entry.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
NgramRL accelerates RL post-training rollouts by using a model-free, prompt-bound n-gram drafter built from recent rollout history, combined with an adaptive fan-out prefetcher to hide CPU lookup latencies.

Why it matters: NgramRL substantially reduces the time and GPU memory costs of RL post-training by accelerating the autoregressive rollout phase, which typically consumes over 70% of total training time.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A data-free on-policy self-training framework enables LLMs and multimodal models to self-improve across domains without external supervision, relying solely on high-level topic descriptions to generate queries and reasoning traces.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that foundation models can unlock and amplify latent capabilities without requiring human-curated prompts, external supervision, or dataset collection.

entry.title: LLaCO: Continuous Diffusion for Large Language Models with Competition-Aware Semantic Scheduling
entry.summary:
LLaCO introduces Competition Threshold Theory and Semantic Retention Scheduling to resolve temporal compression in continuous language diffusion models via spherical noising and rank-decayed scheduling.

Why it matters: It eliminates trajectory misalignment and norm decay in continuous text diffusion models, allowing an 8B continuous model to match discrete diffusion performance.

entry.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
entry.summary:
A new framework evaluates LLM agent performance by disentangling model capabilities from execution harness behaviors using five metrics across 111 evaluation settings and 52,168 trajectories.

Why it matters: Agentic benchmarks reflect joint model-harness behavior, requiring system designers to evaluate component interaction residuals rather than assuming a single harness optimizes performance across all LLMs and tasks.

entry.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Aligning training-side rounding locations with inference in RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm prevents training collapse in BF16 LLM reinforcement learning without modifying kernels, engines, or objectives.

Why it matters: It enables stable on-policy reinforcement learning for LLMs across heterogeneous training and inference stacks by targeting localized numerical precision mismatches rather than requiring expensive full-stack synchronization.

entry.title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation
entry.summary:
This study analyzes Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) as a singular statistical model, evaluating its learning complexity via the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) and forward-backward covariance geometry.

Why it matters: Understanding LoRA's singular geometry and parameter non-identifiability explains why parameter count alone fails to capture the true learning complexity and capacity of adaptors across different network layers.

entry.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the token perceptron model and used the replica method to derive exact generalization bounds and capacity limits based on sequence length, embedding dimension, and discrete vocabulary geometry.

Why it matters: It establishes a theoretical foundation for how embedding dimension, vocabulary geometry, and cross-entropy loss dictate sample complexity and feature learning in token classification tasks.

entry.title: Direction-Aware Token Credit Assignment with Reward-Model Gradients
entry.summary:
Direction-Aware Token Credit Assignment (DATC) improves GRPO by mapping frozen reward-model gradients into policy logit space to weight token updates based on their alignment with the reward gradient direction.

Why it matters: DATC provides a more mathematically aligned token-level credit assignment mechanism for reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) without altering the global response advantage structure.

entry.title: From Parameter Rebasin to Functional Transfer Across Heterogeneous Transformers
entry.summary:
Ariadne is a training-free method that transfers task-specific behavior across heterogeneous Transformers by modeling local activation changes rather than transporting parameters.

Why it matters: It enables efficient reuse of task-specific fine-tuning updates across Transformers of different widths and depths without expensive retrainings or complex parameter-resizing pipelines.

entry.title: Principled Nonlinear Concept Erasure and Steering
entry.summary:
A new conditional autoencoder framework achieves principled nonlinear concept erasure with formal guardedness guarantees while enabling concept steering without target-task labels or extra training costs.

Why it matters: It enables safer AI representations by removing sensitive attributes with theoretical guarantees against nonlinear probes while simultaneously allowing representation steering without sacrificing utility.

entry.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
entry.summary:
BrickWright is a framework using the BrickLayer Python API and physical validity feedback to enable AI coding agents to achieve a 100% physical validity rate when generating LEGO builds from text or image prompts.

Why it matters: It enables pre-trained LLM agents to reliably generate 3D models that can actually be assembled in the real world without requiring dedicated, task-specific model fine-tuning.

entry.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
entry.summary:
Analysis of two diffusion language models reveals that inference cost per token varies significantly by task, language tokenization density, and answer correctness, rather than remaining constant.

Why it matters: Understanding task-dependent computation in diffusion language models allows developers to predict inference costs more accurately and leverage decoding speed as a signal to improve model accuracy.

entry.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
entry.summary:
TARSphere is a full-stack framework featuring a physics simulator with NPCs, an event-driven state machine, an MLLM-driven brain harness, and a 360-episode benchmark for long-horizon embodied agents in dynamic environments.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified platform for testing and improving the physical safety, adaptability, and social coordination of language-model-driven robots in changing real-world environments.

entry.title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research
entry.summary:
SplatLab is an autonomous research system for 3D Gaussian Splatting that reproduces baselines, generates and trains plugin extensions, runs ablations, and writes fully traceably backed manuscripts.

Why it matters: It compresses the months-long manual cycle of reproducing, extending, and documenting 3D Gaussian Splatting research into days of mostly autonomous compute.

entry.title: SEAM: Spectral Embedding Alignment and Merging for Low-Resource TTS
entry.summary:
SEAM is a zero-audio vocabulary expansion method for conditional TTS that constructs new token embeddings using spectral filtering and closed-form ridge regression alignment.

Why it matters: It enables efficient cross-lingual and low-resource adaptation of speech synthesis models by drastically reducing the audio data required to expand model vocabularies.

entry.title: RIPPLE: Recovery Internalization through Process-Level Policy Learning and Effect-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Agentic Coding
entry.summary:
RIPPLE is a recovery-oriented training framework that bridges the critique-to-action handoff gap in long-horizon agentic coding by internalizing process-level teacher guidance into a single self-recovering policy.

Why it matters: It enables LLM coding agents to autonomously self-correct complex execution errors at inference time without relying on external critic models or future-looking supervision during training.

entry.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
entry.summary:
A novel implementation of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy fixes two numerical bugs—Softmax Collapse and Softmax Cancellation—improving gradient stability during training and distillation.

Why it matters: Fixing these fundamental numerical instabilities prevents model drift during knowledge distillation and stabilizes long-term neural network training dynamics.

entry.title: Same Luck, Different Choice: Twin-World Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
TWICE introduces twin-world credit assignment for agentic RL by re-using Gumbel noise across counterfactual rollouts to reduce advantage estimation variance.

Why it matters: By isolating decision impact from downstream stochastic luck, TWICE significantly improves agentic RL performance while cutting the auxiliary compute costs of counterfactual credit assignment.

entry.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
entry.summary:
IQuest-Q1 is an open-source 320B sparse Mixture-of-Experts agentic foundation model (15B active) trained via a three-stage pipeline and model merging to enhance coding and general agentic CLI capabilities.

Why it matters: It provides the open-source community with a large-scale, highly activated-efficient MoE model optimized specifically for complex CLI and coding agent workflows.

entry.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
entry.summary:
EpiSEM-Bench is an executable benchmark evaluating how ten tool-using LLM agents handle unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery when critical facts are omitted from environment responses.

Why it matters: It exposes a critical vulnerability where tool-using LLMs execute unsafe actions due to true but incomplete environmental responses, providing a standardized framework to measure and improve agent robustness.

entry.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
entry.summary:
Evaluating OLMo-3 checkpoints with InstrumentalEval reveals that RLVR causes a nonmonotonic trajectory in instrumental behavior, initially rising before dropping below the SFT baseline at final checkpoints.

Why it matters: The findings challenge the assumption that reinforcement learning monotonically increases dangerous instrumental-convergence subgoals in language models over the course of training.

entry.title: Simulated Control Evals
entry.summary:
Simulated control evaluations (SCEs) use a language model to simulate tool responses, providing more accurate safety predictions for AI deployments than separate executed control settings.

Why it matters: SCEs allow cheap, deployment-specific safety and control evaluations without building complex execution environments, outperforming standard off-environment control benchmarks.

entry.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers used mechanistic interpretability to discover causal subspaces for metaphor in LLMs, enabling direct steering of metaphoricity in both classification and generation tasks.

Why it matters: Mapping and manipulating metaphor-specific subspaces allows researchers to directly control abstract cognitive and stylistic properties in LLM generations.

entry.title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
entry.summary:
A small Qwen3-8B model post-trained with reinforcement learning achieves transferable tool selection across different retrievers and unseen tool corpora, outperforming the much larger Llama-4-Maverick (402B) on ToolBench.

Why it matters: This demonstrates that small open-weights models trained with RL can replace massive proprietary LLMs for multi-step tool selection across scale-constrained tool environments.

entry.title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
entry.summary:
A new coding agent framework introduces Adaptive Skill Granularity, combining a feature-based granularity controller with a finite-state recovery executor to dynamically shift between macro skills and micro-level tool recovery.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that agent skill libraries should be managed as controllable, recoverable execution abstractions rather than simple static retrieval resources, improving robustness in code generation.

entry.title: DIAL: Steerable Language Models with Distilled Instruction-Adherence Levels
entry.summary:
DIAL enables fine-grained numerical control over instruction adherence in LLMs using classifier-free guidance distillation and a text-conditioned, closed-form steering adapter.

Why it matters: It provides a computationally efficient and scalable method to dynamically dial the intensity of LLM traits and constraint adherence without retraining models per instruction.

entry.title: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity
entry.summary:
Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS) formalizes automated agent architecture adaptation under non-stationary shifts as sequential incumbent replacement using risk-constrained graph edits, paired shadow replay, interventional credit assignment, and canary stages.

Why it matters: CMAS provides a safer, risk-bounded approach to automatically reconfiguring multi-agent graph architectures in production environments without requiring manual re-engineering during distribution shifts.

entry.title: Predictable performance is suboptimal, and what it means for model routing
entry.summary:
A study shows performance predictors only outperform a model's self-confidence when the model is suboptimal or the predictor adds significant parameter capacity, with advantages diminishing as models undergo finetuning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that training external routing predictors offers limited benefit over simple model self-confidence unless the base model is uncalibrated, suboptimal, or augmented with significant extra parameter capacity.

entry.title: Same Entity, Different Script: Diagnosing Cross-Script Entity Matching Failures in Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers show that multilingual LLMs fail at cross-script entity matching due to miscalibrated decision criteria rather than lost representation, and locate a middle-layer causal intervention site that restores performance.

Why it matters: Cross-script entity matching failures in LLMs can be mitigated by adjusting internal decision thresholds without retraining or providing additional factual knowledge.

entry.title: HERD: Harness-Evolving Recursive Distillation for Continual Learning
entry.summary:
HERD is a hybrid continual learning framework that combines evolving in-context harness skills with drift-constrained recursive distillation into parameters to minimize catastrophic forgetting.

Why it matters: HERD provides a scalable architecture for lifetime model updating by bridging context-based in-context learning with stable parametric model updates under strict compute budgets.

entry.title: ValuSpec: Plug-and-Play Candidate Valuation before Target Verification for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
ValuSpec is a plug-and-play candidate valuation mechanism that filters low-quality branches from candidate trees prior to target-side verification in tree-based speculative decoding.

Why it matters: It improves LLM inference efficiency by preventing wasteful target-side computation on low-quality tree branches without requiring model retraining or altering decoding accuracy.

entry.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues
entry.summary:
Researchers identify State Integrity Collapse, a phenomenon in long-horizon dialogues where LLMs recall stated instructions but fail to execute them, and introduce the StateTrack-Bench evaluation suite.

Why it matters: Single-turn instruction-following evaluations are insufficient to guarantee LLM reliability, as models frequently stop applying remembered constraints as dialogue state grows.

entry.title: Memory-Aware Reward Modeling: Learning Human Preferences for LLM Memory Use
entry.summary:
Researchers collected ~1,000 pairwise human judgments to evaluate LLM memory use, revealing that users often prefer memory-free responses and that a new memory-aware reward model outperforms baseline evaluators with 72.8% preference prediction accuracy.

Why it matters: Current memory mechanisms and automated benchmarks over-prioritize memory injection, highlighting the need for memory-aware reward models to align retention and context use with actual user preferences.

entry.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
entry.summary:
SpectralCanary is a proactive text-to-image dataset-use auditing method that blends a low-frequency canary image into training data using a smooth low-pass mask without requiring auxiliary models or per-image optimization.

Why it matters: It enables model owners and creators to reliably audit whether proprietary image collections were used to fine-tune text-to-image models with minimal impact on image quality.

entry.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
entry.summary:
BeNice! is a two-stage method combining pretraining stochastic depth with post-training KV-cache broadcasting to enable depth-wise KV-sharing in looped language architectures without losing model quality.

Why it matters: It eliminates the linear KV-cache memory overhead inherent to looped parameter-efficient architectures, significantly reducing latency and memory usage during long-context inference.

entry.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
entry.summary:
FRED improves World Action Models by self-distilling future video representations from noise in a single denoising step using ground-truth targets and historical context.

Why it matters: It enables fast, real-time robot policy inference while significantly improving zero-shot generalization and human-to-robot skill transfer.

entry.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
entry.summary:
FilmFlow is an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into executable 3D camera trajectories by orchestrating multi-agent planning and feedback loop refinement.

Why it matters: FilmFlow bridges the gap between high-level cinematographic intent and executable 3D camera trajectories, enabling automated, controllable virtual film production.

entry.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
entry.summary:
A study quantifies 'mosaic effect' confidentiality leaks in LLM agents, where models infer and disclose forbidden composite conclusions from accessible documents even under benign queries and explicit aggregation safeguards.

Why it matters: LLM agents operating in mixed-clearance environments present a structural data leak risk by inferring sensitive conclusions from unclassified documents, which standard classification headers and refusals fail to fully mitigate.

entry.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
entry.summary:
Raw-RAG outperforms complex agentic memory systems across multiple long-term conversation benchmarks by leveraging dense retrieval and reranking directly over raw, unmutated conversation histories.

Why it matters: This demonstrates that complex, resource-intensive agentic memory operations are often unnecessary, making naive RAG a crucial baseline for long-term LLM conversation tasks.

entry.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary:
RLSplat is a resource-linear feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that reduces inference latency, peak memory, and output size proportionally with lower target Gaussian budgets.

Why it matters: It enables deployable feed-forward 3D reconstruction on memory-constrained edge devices by scaling inference computation and memory directly with the allocated Gaussian budget.

entry.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
entry.summary:
TTR-Compressor introduces sequence compression via end-to-end learned test-time regression, computing compressed token coefficients in closed form during the forward pass.

Why it matters: It offers a more parameter-efficient compression primitive that significantly reduces token counts in multimodal LLMs and sparse attention without sacrificing performance.

entry.title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos
entry.summary:
Verus-Insight improves AI-generated video detection by decomposing artifact analysis into Inspection Planning, Evidence Verification, and Evidence Aggregation using progressive capability training.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured, explainable framework for deepfake and synthetic video detection that grounds final classification decisions in verified visual evidence rather than opaque heuristics.

entry.title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark
entry.summary:
AnyGameRenderer is a video-to-video generative rendering model that turns low-fidelity game blockouts into high-quality video while maintaining strict entity-level correspondence and layout timing.

Why it matters: It enables AI agents to generate visual assets for diverse game genres without losing precise control over spatial layout, entity counts, or object timing.

entry.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
entry.summary:
AgentVQA is a unified offline benchmark containing 1,000 real-world examples across five agent domains, designed to evaluate vision-language models on complex agentic visual understanding.

Why it matters: It offers a scalable, low-cost offline benchmark that accurately mirrors online agent performance while pinpointing visual state representation as the primary failure mode in current vision-language models.

entry.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
T2Quant is a novel framework for Diffusion Language Models that optimizes mixed-precision activation quantization by dynamically allocating bit-widths based on label-free task and timestep sensitivity signals.

Why it matters: It enables higher accuracy and efficiency in DLM inference by dynamically targeting precision where and when it is most needed without requiring labeled evaluation data.

entry.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
A study reveals that reasoning models inherit the "{wait}" pause marker from training data rather than inventing it via reinforcement learning, showing large RL accuracy gains can occur entirely without the word.

Why it matters: Marker frequency is an unreliable indicator of RL-driven reasoning, highlighting that model behaviors attributed to RL discovery may simply be artifacts inherited from supervised pre-training or fine-tuning datasets.

entry.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
entry.summary:
RIDAR is a new framework that uses the 14-type RIVT taxonomy to detect research integrity violations in autonomous agents post-hoc and dynamically correct them during runtime.

Why it matters: It enables automated safeguards to prevent autonomous AI research agents from producing unfaithful, unreproducible, or invalid scientific outputs.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
A controlled study on diffusion language models reveals optimal unmasking policy design choices, resulting in an 856K-parameter policy that achieves superior speed-accuracy trade-offs across multiple benchmarks.

Why it matters: Using lightweight learned unmasking policies with the right supervision targets and input features accelerates diffusion language model inference while maintaining output quality.

entry.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
entry.summary:
F2G-Pose is a real-time, single-pass RGB-D framework that directly predicts category-level 3D pose, metric size, and shape completion at 28 FPS.

Why it matters: It eliminates high-latency diffusion sampling and multi-stage error propagation, enabling fast and accurate category-level 3D pose estimation for real-time robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Who Takes the Lead? Model Ability and Task-Conditioned Collaboration with Humans
entry.summary:
A study using a shared-control maze reveals that stronger language-model agents dynamically condition human involvement on route advantage, while weaker models lack this selective task allocation.

Why it matters: A drop in human interaction by AI agents indicates an optimal division of labor based on relative capability rather than a breakdown in collaboration.

entry.title: Multi-Token Prediction and Alternative Tokenization Improve Learning Latent Multi-Hop Graph Search at Scale
entry.summary:
Researchers overcome graph pathfinding failure modes in language models by identifying supervision signal and tokenization as orthogonal bottlenecks and solving them via multi-token prediction and alternative tokenization methods.

Why it matters: Combining multi-token prediction with optimized tokenizations enables language models to reliably perform complex multi-hop algorithmic reasoning over large unseen graph structures.

entry.title: SQuAT: Spherical Lattice Vector Quantization-Aware Training
entry.summary:
SQuAT scales lattice VQ-QAT to multi-billion-parameter LLMs by using separate straight-through estimators for decomposed weight directions and magnitudes alongside a distributed exact nearest-neighbor assignment scheme.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that lattice-based vector quantization can be efficiently trained at scale via quantization-aware training, enabling state-of-the-art accuracy for highly compressed low-bit LLMs.

entry.title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced RMT-Jailbreak, a framework that transfers autoregressive jailbreak attacks to diffusion language models by turning harmful responses into masked templates for bidirectional reconstruction.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that safety alignments in diffusion LLMs can be bypassed by repurposing output templates from autoregressive LLMs, exposing a critical cross-architecture vulnerability.

entry.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization
entry.summary:
OPTIC compresses Per-Layer Embeddings up to 1,002x by storing one quantized code tuple per token and using layer-specific affine decoders fitted to the output path.

Why it matters: OPTIC enables massive reductions in GPU memory overhead for per-layer embedding architectures with negligible throughput loss and high performance retention.

entry.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
entry.summary:
Cola2 introduces a hierarchical language modeling framework using dynamic continuous semantic compression and a block-causal masked diffusion decoder, demonstrating strong performance and unsaturated scaling compared to standard autoregressive models.

Why it matters: Cola2 proves that continuous-latent hierarchical generation can match or exceed massive autoregressive baselines like Llama-3-8B while utilizing a fraction of the pretraining compute budget.

entry.title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering
entry.summary:
A comparative study reveals Transformers exhibit a context-beginning position bias absent in pure state-space models, though both families maintain a context-ending bias in long-context question answering.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that position bias varies by model family, prompt structure, and attention allocation helps engineers better optimize context layout and architecture choices for long-document tasks.

entry.title: Delta N-gram: Forward-Only Continual Writing into a Language Model's Native N-gram Memory
entry.summary:
Delta N-gram introduces a forward-only continual write path into a language model's frozen native hashed N-gram table using a 4.1M-parameter writer to emit gated target updates into a sparse delta patch.

Why it matters: It enables rapid, stable, and reversible continual knowledge updates in language models without requiring backpropagation or catastrophic forgetting of base capabilities.

entry.title: RIFT: KV Cache Compression for Draft Models with Complementary Compressibility Training
entry.summary:
RIFT introduces adaptive KV cache refreshing and sparse-attention compressibility training to mitigate decode staleness in speculative decoding draft models.

Why it matters: It dramatically reduces memory consumption during long-output speculative decoding without sacrificing the acceptance rate or speedup of the draft model.

entry.title: What Pairwise Evaluation Misses: Reward Scores across Prompts
entry.summary:
A study reveals pairwise evaluation masks prompt-level reward model errors, showing models over-cluster scores by prompt (shares of 0.34 to 0.64 on HelpSteer2) compared to near-zero human rating variation.

Why it matters: Evaluating reward models solely via pairwise comparisons hides prompt-level score distortions, requiring separate audits for between-prompt variation, prompt sensitivity, and global selection utility.

entry.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
METTA is a meta-reinforcement learning framework that decomposes fast adaptation into linear-complexity within-episode causal neural memory and compact cross-episode summaries for efficient long-context task inference.

Why it matters: It enables meta-RL agents to efficiently adapt to unseen long-context tasks without suffering from the quadratic computational and memory costs of transformer architectures.
